frames.cefr: Nível A1 (QECR): entende e usa expressões cotidianas muito simples para necessidades imediatas. Meta de desempenho, não certificação.

frames.title: A Saturday at the mall · 1/3
paragraphs: Last Saturday, my friend Rosa and I went to the **mall** in **Houston**. It was hot outside, but inside the mall it was cool. There were people, music and shops everywhere.

We walked past many shops. Suddenly Rosa stopped. "Look at this bag! It's so cute," she said. It was small and red. "**How much is it?**" I asked. "**It's fifty dollars**," she said. That is not **cheap**.
frames.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

frames.title: A Saturday at the mall · 2/3
paragraphs: Then I saw a sign: **30% off**. "**Is it on sale?**" I asked. "**Yes, thirty percent off**," said the clerk. Thirty percent of fifty is fifteen, so the new **price** was thirty-five dollars. "**That's a good price**," I said. Rosa agreed. "**I'll take it.**"
At the register, the clerk asked, "**Cash or card?**" Rosa said, "Card, please." She got a **receipt**. "Keep it," I said. "You can return the bag with the receipt if you want."

frames.title: A Saturday at the mall · 3/3
paragraphs: I saw a jacket, too. It was perfect, but it was very **expensive**: one hundred and twenty dollars! I said, "**Maybe later.**" My friend smiled. "**Retail therapy!**" she said.
We ended the day with a big juice in the food court. We spent a little, but we had a great time. "**Thanks for coming in!**" said the clerk as we left.

frames.title: Como ensinar leitura e escrita
frames.goal: Ao final, o aluno entende a ideia e os detalhes de um texto sobre “At the mall” e escreve 2 ou 3 frases suas.

steps.d: Previsão: com 3 palavras do glossário, os alunos adivinham a história.
Uma pessoa lê um parágrafo e a outra resume em uma frase.
Perguntas de verdadeiro ou falso com correção: o aluno corrige a frase falsa.
Bilhete ou mensagem de 20 a 30 palavras usando a estrutura do dia.

errors: Esquecer o -s da terceira pessoa: “He work here.” Peça para o aluno marcar o -s com a mão quando ele aparece.
Pronúncia do -ed: /t/, /d/ ou /ɪd/ (walked, played, wanted). Português costuma pronunciar um “e” a mais.
Colocar to depois do modal: “Can you to help me?”. Depois de can, o verbo vem sem to.
frames.adapt: Turma mais rápida: peça um parágrafo de 4 frases. Turma que precisa de apoio: dê o início das frases e leia o texto em coro antes.

frames.title: Ler e escrever no formato TOEFL
tip: O TOEFL cobra leitura rápida (palavras incompletas, avisos do dia a dia, textos acadêmicos) e escrita com precisão (montar frases, e-mail, discussão).
